messages:
michael: FYI we just received a $48,750 vendor credit from CloudRack for Feb usage that posted after the Feb month-end. It was for a billing dispute; vendor adjusted the invoice today. How should we treat this for revrec and the Feb accruals?

sana: Is this a credit that reduces cost of goods sold or is it a bill-rate correction that reduces hosting expense? Do we have the original invoice # and GL mappings? :thinking:

michael: Invoice 987654, vendor memo says 'usage overcharge reversal'. AP applied as credit to vendor account not as cash refund. Attached PDF in the ticket. I think it relates to hosted GPU bill that we accrued for Feb.

elaine: If it reduces hosting expense, technically expense should be adjusted in the period the expense was recognized (Feb). Since the credit came after close, we either 1) post a prior-period adjustment (if material) or 2) reverse the Feb accrual and record a current-period credit against expense with explanation. Need controller sign-off.

michael: Not material by policy (materiality threshold $250k). Can we do a simple reclassification? What journal would you book?

elaine: Proposed flow:
- Reverse the Feb accrual that estimated the invoice (debit Accrued Expenses, credit Hosting Expense).
- Post the vendor credit to reduce Hosting Expense in Mar but tag it as a Feb true-up in the memo so internal reports can reflect net Feb spend.

sana: Example journals:```
1) Reverse accrual (Feb accrual reversal posted Mar):
   Dr Accrued Expenses 48,750
   Cr Hosting Expense 48,750

2) Record vendor credit receipt (Mar):
   Dr Accounts Payable - CloudRack 48,750
   Cr Hosting Expense 48,750
```
Then AP clears when credit applies. We should also update the Feb accrual roll-forward spreadsheet to show the reversal and attach vendor PDF.

michael: That looks good. Is there any revrec impact? This is a hosting vendor credit not customer revenue, correct?

elaine: Correct — no revenue impact. It's an expense vendor credit, so it doesn't touch deferred revenue or recognized revenue schedules. Just ensure we don't double-count the benefit in unit economics reports: update the monthly cost-of-inference dashboard note.

accrual-bot: Reminder: when reversing accruals, include original accrual id in the memo field and file a supporting doc in Finance Drive under /Accruals/2026/Feb_reversals/

michael: @tom can you approve the reversal and the AP posting flow?

tom: Reviewed. Approve the two-step approach. Post reversal against Accrued Expenses and then record the vendor credit in AP as Jana recommended. Please include the vendor memo and ticket link in the journal attachment. :thumbsup:

elaine: I'll prepare JEs and update the accrual tracker. tagging the GLs: 5300 Hosting Expense, 2100 Accrued Expenses, 2001 AP CloudRack. I'll put 'Vendor credit — Feb usage true-up' in the memo and route to Tom for final sign-off in NetSuite.

sana: I'll update the P&L anomaly tracker and add a note to the March cost reconciliation that this is a post-close vendor credit.

michael: Thanks all. Closing the loop — posting will happen today, I'll update this thread with the JE numbers and link to the NetSuite journal once posted.

michael: JE posted: Journal 2026-03-4567 (accrual reversal) and Journal 2026-03-4568 (AP credit). NetSuite links: https://redwood-ns.company/journal/2026-03-4567 , https://redwood-ns.company/journal/2026-03-4568

elaine: Confirmed both JEs and attached vendor PDF to both journals. Closing here. :white_check_mark:
